en: whereas; where; in cases where; if
ex: Il Nord ha recuperato i livelli pre-crisi, laddove il Sud arranca ancora.
exEn: The North has recovered pre-crisis levels, whereas the South is still struggling.
note: Two uses: adversative ('whereas', indicative) and conditional/legal ('laddove sia necessario' = where necessary, subjunctive). Formal register.

en: if; in the event that; should
ex: Qualora il pagamento non pervenisse entro trenta giorni, il contratto si intenderà risolto.
exEn: Should payment not be received within thirty days, the contract will be deemed terminated.
note: Always with the subjunctive (present or imperfect). Formal alternative to 'se' and 'nel caso in cui', typical of contracts and notices.

en: in order to; so as to; whence (lit.)
ex: Si prega di confermare la presenza onde evitare inutili sprechi.
exEn: Please confirm attendance in order to avoid unnecessary waste.
note: 'Onde' + infinitive = 'in order to' (bureaucratic); 'onde evitare' is the fixed phrase. As a relative adverb ('whence, by which') it is archaic. Homograph of 'onde' = waves.

ex: L'istanza è stata presentata fuori termine e pertanto non può essere accolta.
exEn: The application was filed late and therefore cannot be accepted.
note: Formal written connector; 'quindi' and 'perciò' are the neutral equivalents. Do not confuse with 'per tanto' (for so much).

ex: Non ha vinto, ma perlomeno ha dimostrato di poter competere ad alto livello.
exEn: She did not win, but at least she showed she can compete at the top level.
note: Also written 'per lo meno'. Slightly more formal than 'almeno'; 'quantomeno' is a close synonym.

en: moreover; incidentally; for that matter; however
ex: La misura, peraltro già sperimentata in Francia, entrerà in vigore a gennaio.
exEn: The measure, which incidentally has already been tried in France, will come into force in January.
note: Adds a side remark that qualifies the statement; often slightly concessive. Very frequent in journalism and legal prose, rare in speech.

ex: La crisi ha colpito finanche i settori tradizionalmente più solidi.
exEn: The crisis has hit even the traditionally most solid sectors.
note: Literary/southern variant of 'perfino', 'persino'. Also 'financo'.

ex: Si veda l'articolo 5 del regolamento e le norme ivi richiamate.
exEn: See article 5 of the regulation and the rules referred to therein.
note: Legal and academic; 'ivi compreso' = including. In footnotes 'ivi' = same work, different page (vs 'ibidem' = same work, same page).

ex: Si prega codesto ufficio di trasmettere la documentazione richiesta.
exEn: That office is requested to forward the documentation requested.
note: Third demonstrative of the classic system (questo/codesto/quello), now confined to Tuscan speech and bureaucratic letters addressing the recipient's institution. Forms: codesto/a/i/e.

ex: Le suddette condizioni si applicano a tutti i contratti stipulati dopo il primo gennaio.
exEn: The aforementioned conditions apply to all contracts signed after the first of January.
note: Bureaucratic; synonyms 'sopraccitato', 'summenzionato', 'predetto', 'di cui sopra'. Can be used as a noun ('il suddetto' = the person mentioned).

ex: Non è lecito arricchirsi con il lavoro altrui.
exEn: It is not right to get rich on other people's work.
note: Invariable possessive placed after the noun ('la roba altrui', 'i diritti altrui'). As a pronoun: 'l'altrui' (literary) = others' property; 'a spese altrui' = at others' expense.

ex: Taluni sostengono che la riforma sia stata scritta su misura per pochi.
exEn: Some maintain that the reform was tailor-made for a few.
note: Formal/literary; forms taluno/a/i/e. As a determiner: 'in taluni casi' = in certain cases. Neutral: 'alcuni', 'qualcuno'.

ex: Non intendo rendere conto delle mie scelte a chicchessia.
exEn: I do not intend to account for my choices to anyone whatsoever.
note: Emphatic indefinite, typically in negative sentences. Invariable. Compare 'checché' ('checché se ne dica' = whatever people say).

en: by virtue of; on the strength of; under (a law)
ex: In virtù dell'accordo, i lavoratori distaccati mantengono la retribuzione del paese d'origine.
exEn: By virtue of the agreement, posted workers keep the pay of their country of origin.
note: Formal causal preposition; synonyms 'grazie a', 'per effetto di', 'in forza di' (legal).

en: by way of exception to; notwithstanding; in derogation from
ex: In deroga al regolamento, il termine è stato prorogato di dieci giorni.
exEn: By way of exception to the regulation, the deadline was extended by ten days.
note: Legal-administrative; noun 'deroga' (exemption), verb 'derogare a'. 'Inderogabile' = mandatory, non-negotiable.

en: pursuant to; under; in accordance with (a law)
ex: Ai sensi dell'articolo 13 del Regolamento, la informiamo che i suoi dati saranno trattati con modalità informatiche.
exEn: Pursuant to article 13 of the Regulation, we inform you that your data will be processed electronically.
note: The most common legal citation formula; also 'ai sensi e per gli effetti di'. 'Senso' here = meaning/scope of the provision.

ex: In seno alla maggioranza si sono aperte profonde divisioni sulla riforma.
exEn: Deep divisions over the reform have opened up within the majority.
note: Formal/journalistic ('in seno al partito, alla commissione'); literally 'in the bosom of'. Neutral: 'all'interno di'.

en: without prejudice to; except for; subject to
ex: Fatto salvo quanto previsto dall'articolo 3, le parti possono recedere in qualsiasi momento.
exEn: Without prejudice to the provisions of article 3, the parties may withdraw at any time.
note: Agrees with the noun: 'fatta salva la facoltà', 'fatti salvi i diritti acquisiti'. 'Salvo' alone + noun is a lighter equivalent.

en: in this particular case; in the case in point
ex: La legge tutela i consumatori, e nella fattispecie chi acquista online.
exEn: The law protects consumers, and in this particular case those who buy online.
note: Formal specifier, from the legal noun 'fattispecie'. Often used loosely to mean 'namely, specifically'.

en: by way of; as (a); for the purpose of
ex: Le fu versata una somma a titolo di risarcimento per il danno subito.
exEn: She was paid a sum by way of compensation for the damage suffered.
note: Many fixed phrases: 'a titolo di esempio' (by way of example), 'a titolo gratuito/oneroso' (free of charge / for consideration), 'a titolo personale' (in a personal capacity).

ex: Ove possibile, si prediliga la trasmissione per via telematica.
exEn: Where possible, electronic transmission is to be preferred.
note: Formal/legal; 'ove necessario', 'ove occorra'. Also relative adverb 'where' in literary prose ('la casa ove nacque'). Compare 'laddove', 'qualora'.

ex: Il rapporto contiene un'attenta disamina delle cause del fallimento.
exEn: The report contains a careful examination of the causes of the bankruptcy.
note: Formal; 'fare/condurre una disamina di'. Stress: disàmina. Verb 'disaminare' is rare; 'esaminare' is normal.

ex: Il manoscritto è ricco di postille autografe dell'autore.
exEn: The manuscript is full of the author's own marginal notes.
note: Also 'una postilla' = a short final remark in a speech or article. Verb 'postillare' = to annotate. Distinct from 'poscritto' (P.S.).

ex: È ricorso a una lunga perifrasi per non pronunciare la parola 'licenziamento'.
exEn: He resorted to a long circumlocution to avoid saying the word 'dismissal'.
note: Invariable. In grammar 'perifrasi verbale' = verbal periphrasis ('stare per fare'). Compare 'giro di parole' (colloquial).

ex: Il suo ragionamento è un sillogismo zoppo: la premessa maggiore è falsa.
exEn: His reasoning is a flawed syllogism: the major premise is false.
note: 'Premessa maggiore/minore', 'conclusione'. Figuratively for any mechanical or specious reasoning; 'sillogistico' adj.

ex: La diatriba tra i due storici sulle origini del fascismo dura da vent'anni.
exEn: The dispute between the two historians over the origins of Fascism has lasted twenty years.
note: Stress on -trì-: diatrìba (also diàtriba, more learned). In Italian it means a two-sided quarrel, not a one-sided harangue as in English.

ex: Il suo discorso era pieno di sottintesi che solo gli addetti ai lavori potevano cogliere.
exEn: His speech was full of implications that only insiders could grasp.
note: Also adjective/participle: 'soggetto sottinteso' = implied subject; 'è sottinteso che' = it goes without saying that. 'Parlare per sottintesi' = to speak in hints.

ex: Il diniego del permesso di soggiorno può essere impugnato entro sessanta giorni.
exEn: The refusal of the residence permit may be challenged within sixty days.
note: Formal/administrative noun for 'rifiuto'; 'opporre un diniego' = to refuse. 'Silenzio-diniego' = refusal by administrative silence.

ex: Le previsioni sul prezzo del petrolio restano quanto mai aleatorie.
exEn: Forecasts of the oil price remain as uncertain as ever.
note: From Latin 'alea' (dice); 'contratto aleatorio' in law = contract whose outcome depends on chance (insurance). Not 'random' in the statistical sense ('casuale').

ex: Con un'osservazione arguta ha sciolto la tensione della riunione.
exEn: With a witty remark he dissolved the tension in the meeting.
note: Noun 'arguzia' (wit, witticism). Implies quick intelligence plus humour; 'spiritoso' is merely funny.

ex: Le sue recensioni caustiche erano temute da tutti i registi.
exEn: His caustic reviews were feared by every director.
note: Literal sense: 'soda caustica'. Figurative synonyms: 'mordace', 'pungente', 'sferzante', 'sarcastico'.

ex: La notizia ha avuto un effetto dirompente sugli equilibri della coalizione.
exEn: The news had an explosive effect on the balance within the coalition.
note: Originally military ('proiettile dirompente'); now the standard rendering of 'disruptive' in business language ('innovazione dirompente').

ex: Il successo del partito si è rivelato effimero: alle elezioni successive è scomparso.
exEn: The party's success proved short-lived: at the next election it vanished.
note: Stress: effìmero. Also a noun: 'l'effimero' = the transient, the culture of the ephemeral (1970s-80s cultural policy in Rome).

ex: Con un margine così esiguo, la maggioranza rischia di cadere a ogni voto.
exEn: With such a slender margin, the majority risks falling at every vote.
note: Formal; 'esiguità' noun. Collocates with 'numero', 'somma', 'margine', 'minoranza'. Neutral: 'scarso', 'piccolo'.

ex: Il sentiero diventa impervio dopo il rifugio e richiede attrezzatura da roccia.
exEn: The path becomes rugged after the refuge and requires climbing equipment.
note: Literal (terrain) and figurative ('una strada impervia verso la riforma'). Not to be confused with 'imperioso' (imperious).

ex: Il suo commento fu lapidario: «Non se ne parla nemmeno».
exEn: His comment was terse: 'Out of the question'.
note: From 'lapide' (gravestone): concise as an inscription. Praise for brevity; noun 'lapidarietà'.

en: hard to digest; difficult; forbidding (of a subject, text)
ex: La materia è ostica anche per gli studenti più preparati.
exEn: The subject is tough going even for the best-prepared students.
note: Stress: òstico. Used of intellectual difficulty and unpleasant tasks, not of physical hardness ('duro'). Compare 'arduo', 'complesso'.

ex: Una traduzione pedissequa tradisce il testo tanto quanto una troppo libera.
exEn: A slavish translation betrays the text as much as an overly free one.
note: From Latin 'pedisequus', a servant walking behind. Collocations: 'imitazione/ripetizione/applicazione pedissequa'.

ex: Ha scelto un titolo pregnante che condensa il tema dell'intero saggio.
exEn: She chose a meaningful title that condenses the theme of the whole essay.
note: False friend: not 'pregnant' (incinta). Noun 'pregnanza'. Also 'nel senso più pregnante del termine' = in the fullest sense of the word.

ex: Con una fuga rocambolesca è riuscito a evitare la cattura per tre giorni.
exEn: With a hair-raising escape he managed to avoid capture for three days.
note: From Rocambole, hero of 19th-century French adventure novels. Typical of sports and crime reporting ('rimonta rocambolesca', 'evasione rocambolesca').

ex: Un osservatore sagace avrebbe notato che i conti non tornavano già da tempo.
exEn: A shrewd observer would have noticed that the accounts had not added up for some time.
note: Noun 'sagacia'. Positive; compare 'scaltro' (cunning, more ambivalent), 'astuto', 'perspicace'.

ex: È sconcertante che nessuno abbia verificato i dati prima della pubblicazione.
exEn: It is baffling that no one checked the data before publication.
note: Verb 'sconcertare', noun 'sconcerto'. Stronger than 'sorprendente'; often expresses disapproval.

ex: È una forma subdola di censura: nessun divieto esplicito, ma la paura di parlare.
exEn: It is an insidious form of censorship: no explicit ban, but the fear of speaking.
note: Stress: sùbdolo. Of people and things ('una malattia subdola' = a disease with hidden symptoms). Synonyms: 'insidioso', 'sornione' (milder, sly-humorous).

ex: Dopo un anno di riforme i risultati tangibili sono ancora pochi.
exEn: After a year of reforms the tangible results are still few.
note: 'Beni tangibili/intangibili' in accounting; 'un segno tangibile' = a concrete sign. Opposite 'intangibile'.

ex: I volontari lavorarono alacremente per tutta la notte per contenere l'acqua.
exEn: The volunteers worked energetically all night to hold back the water.
note: Adjective 'alacre' (brisk, eager), noun 'alacrità'. Formal; conveys energetic enthusiasm in work.

ex: Il manuale è stato seguito pedissequamente, senza adattarlo al contesto locale.
exEn: The manual was followed slavishly, without adapting it to the local context.
note: Always pejorative. Collocates with 'seguire', 'copiare', 'applicare', 'ripetere'.

ex: Il reperto risale verosimilmente al terzo secolo avanti Cristo.
exEn: The find dates in all likelihood from the third century BC.
note: Cautious formal hedge, typical of academic and forensic prose. Near-synonyms: 'presumibilmente', 'con ogni probabilità'.

ex: La villa sorge in una località amena sulle colline del Chianti.
exEn: The villa stands in a delightful spot in the Chianti hills.
note: Literary of places ('luogo ameno'); of people or remarks often ironic ('un tipo ameno' = a funny character). 'Letteratura amena' = light reading.

ex: Le sanzioni sono state troppo blande per avere un effetto dissuasivo.
exEn: The sanctions were too mild to have a deterrent effect.
note: False friend: not 'bland' in the sense of tasteless ('insipido'). Verb 'blandire' = to coax, flatter.

ex: È una domanda capziosa: qualunque risposta mi metterebbe nei guai.
exEn: It is a trick question: any answer would get me into trouble.
note: From Latin 'captio', trap. 'Domanda capziosa' = loaded/trick question; 'argomento capzioso' = specious argument.

ex: L'incertezza normativa ha effetti deleteri sugli investimenti.
exEn: Regulatory uncertainty has harmful effects on investment.
note: Formal; stronger than 'dannoso'. Synonyms: 'nocivo', 'pernicioso'.

ex: Alcune espressioni del testo sono ormai desuete e vanno spiegate agli studenti.
exEn: Some expressions in the text are now obsolete and need to be explained to students.
note: Noun 'desuetudine' ('caduto in desuetudine' = fallen into disuse). Of words, customs, laws; 'obsoleto' is preferred for technology.

ex: L'elenco non è esaustivo, ma copre i casi più frequenti.
exEn: The list is not exhaustive, but it covers the most frequent cases.
note: Also 'esauriente' (of an answer or explanation: full, satisfactory). Adverb 'esaustivamente'.

ex: Gli studenti fanno lezione in un edificio fatiscente, con infiltrazioni e intonaco cadente.
exEn: The students have lessons in a dilapidated building, with leaks and crumbling plaster.
note: Of buildings and structures; figuratively of institutions. From Latin 'fatiscere', to fall apart.

ex: Le società fittizie servivano a far transitare i fondi all'estero.
exEn: The shell companies served to move the funds abroad.
note: 'Residenza fittizia', 'matrimonio fittizio'. Not 'fictional' in the literary sense ('di finzione', 'immaginario').

ex: Le prove a suo carico sono inconfutabili: le immagini lo riprendono chiaramente.
exEn: The evidence against him is irrefutable: the footage shows him clearly.
note: From 'confutare'. Synonyms: 'incontrovertibile', 'inoppugnabile', 'inequivocabile'.

ex: Il risarcimento offerto è irrisorio rispetto al danno subito.
exEn: The compensation offered is derisory compared with the damage suffered.
note: From 'irridere' (to mock): so small it is an insult. Collocates with 'prezzo', 'somma', 'cifra', 'pena'.

ex: Il confine tra satira e diffamazione è sempre più labile.
exEn: The boundary between satire and defamation is increasingly blurred.
note: 'Memoria labile' = poor memory; 'labilità emotiva' = emotional instability. Not 'liable'.

ex: La ricostruzione dei fatti resta lacunosa in più punti.
exEn: The reconstruction of the events remains patchy at several points.
note: From 'lacuna' (gap). Of knowledge, documentation, legislation ('normativa lacunosa').

ex: Il conflitto di interessi è lampante, eppure nessuno lo ha sollevato.
exEn: The conflict of interest is glaring, and yet no one raised it.
note: From 'lampa' (lamp): clear as daylight. 'Un esempio lampante', 'una prova lampante'. Also 'olio lampante' = lamp oil (non-edible olive oil).

ex: La procedura di rimborso è talmente macchinosa che molti rinunciano.
exEn: The refund procedure is so cumbersome that many give up.
note: From 'macchina': works like an over-engineered machine. Of procedures, plots, reasoning. Synonym 'farraginoso'.

ex: La relazione è prolissa: le stesse conclusioni potevano stare in due pagine.
exEn: The report is long-winded: the same conclusions could have fitted in two pages.
note: Noun 'prolissità'. Opposite 'conciso', 'lapidario', 'stringato'.

ex: Non riesco a capire quale sia il motivo recondito di tanta ostilità.
exEn: I cannot understand what the hidden reason for so much hostility is.
note: Stress: recòndito. Literary; 'i più reconditi segreti', 'le pieghe più recondite dell'animo'.

ex: Il medico è stato sbrigativo e non ha nemmeno guardato le analisi.
exEn: The doctor was brusque and did not even look at the test results.
note: From 'sbrigare' (to get something done). Usually mildly negative (too quick); 'spiccio' is the colloquial near-synonym.

ex: C'è un contrasto stridente tra il lusso del quartier generale e i salari degli operai.
exEn: There is a glaring contrast between the luxury of the headquarters and the workers' wages.
note: From 'stridere' (to screech; figuratively to clash). 'Contrasto/contraddizione stridente' are the main collocations.

ex: Il tempo a disposizione si riduceva inesorabilmente mentre la commissione discuteva.
exEn: The time available shrank inexorably while the committee debated.
note: Adjective 'inesorabile' (unrelenting, unstoppable). Frequent with 'avanzare', 'scivolare', 'declinare'.

ex: Le somme indebitamente percepite dovranno essere restituite con gli interessi.
exEn: The sums improperly received will have to be returned with interest.
note: Legal-administrative; adjective 'indebito' ('indebita percezione', 'arricchimento indebito'). Unrelated to 'indebitarsi' (to get into debt).

en: thoroughly; extensively; down to the smallest unit
ex: Il servizio è diffuso capillarmente su tutto il territorio, anche nei paesi più piccoli.
exEn: The service is spread extensively across the whole territory, even in the smallest villages.
note: From 'capillare' (capillary): reaching everywhere like blood vessels. 'Distribuzione capillare', 'controllo capillare' are typical collocations.

it: avere la puzza sotto il naso
en: be stuck-up; look down one's nose at people
ex: Da quando è stata promossa ha la puzza sotto il naso e non saluta più nessuno.
exEn: Since she was promoted she has been stuck-up and no longer greets anyone.
note: Colloquial, pejorative. Image: walking with the nose in the air as if everything smelled bad. Synonym 'essere altezzoso', 'snob'.

en: be taken completely by surprise; act as if one knew nothing
ex: Quando gli hanno chiesto dei conti mancanti è caduto dalle nuvole, ma nessuno gli ha creduto.
exEn: When they asked him about the missing accounts he acted amazed, but no one believed him.
note: Often implies feigned surprise. Compare 'cascare dalle nuvole' (same meaning, more colloquial) and 'restare di stucco' (genuine astonishment).

en: be a big shot; be a bigwig
ex: Suo zio è un pezzo grosso al ministero: una sua telefonata sblocca qualsiasi pratica.
exEn: His uncle is a big shot at the ministry: one phone call from him unblocks any file.
note: Colloquial; also 'pezzo da novanta' (from the calibre of a cannon, Sicilian mafia usage). Neutral: 'una persona influente'.

en: raise hell; kick up a tremendous fuss
ex: I residenti hanno fatto il diavolo a quattro finché il Comune non ha ritirato il progetto.
exEn: The residents raised hell until the council withdrew the project.
note: From medieval mystery plays with four devils on stage. Can also mean to make a great effort to obtain something.

en: beat about the bush; stall; keep putting something off
ex: Smettila di menare il can per l'aia e dimmi se accetti l'offerta o no.
exEn: Stop beating about the bush and tell me whether you accept the offer or not.
note: Image: leading the dog round and round the threshing floor ('aia'). 'Menare' = to lead (archaic) or to hit (colloquial).

ex: Quando ha annunciato le dimissioni, tutta la redazione è rimasta di stucco.
exEn: When he announced his resignation, the whole newsroom was dumbfounded.
note: Image: as still as a stucco statue. Also 'restare di stucco', 'di sasso', 'a bocca aperta'.

en: slip away; make oneself scarce; run off
ex: Appena ha visto arrivare il creditore ha tagliato la corda dal retro.
exEn: As soon as he saw the creditor arrive he slipped out the back.
note: Nautical origin (cutting the mooring rope). Colloquial synonyms: 'svignarsela', 'darsela a gambe', 'filarsela'.

en: be involved in everything; have a finger in every pie; have inside influence
ex: Chiedi a Marco: ha le mani in pasta in tutti gli appalti della provincia.
exEn: Ask Marco: he has a finger in every pie when it comes to contracts in the province.
note: Often suggests questionable influence. Do not confuse with 'mettere le mani avanti' (to cover oneself in advance).

en: make a blunder; get it badly wrong
ex: I giornali hanno preso un granchio: la persona arrestata era un omonimo.
exEn: The newspapers got it badly wrong: the person arrested was a namesake.
note: From fishing (hooking a crab instead of a fish). Colloquial; 'prendere un abbaglio' is the near-synonym for a misperception.

en: clutch at straws; use far-fetched arguments to defend a lost cause
ex: L'avvocato si arrampicava sugli specchi per giustificare le contraddizioni del suo cliente.
exEn: The lawyer was clutching at straws to justify his client's contradictions.
note: Image: trying to climb a mirror, an impossible and ridiculous effort. Used of defensive argumentation.

en: turn a deaf ear; pretend not to hear
ex: Il governo ha fatto orecchie da mercante alle richieste dei pensionati.
exEn: The government turned a deaf ear to the pensioners' demands.
note: Merchants supposedly heard only what suited them. Construction: 'fare orecchie da mercante a qualcosa'.

en: have a guilty conscience; be touchy because one has something to hide
ex: Nessuno lo aveva accusato, ma si è difeso subito: chi ha la coda di paglia si scotta facilmente.
exEn: No one had accused him, but he defended himself at once: a guilty conscience needs no accuser.
note: A straw tail catches fire easily, so the animal keeps away from flames. Used of people who react defensively to innocent remarks.

en: throw in the towel; give up
ex: Dopo il terzo rifiuto della banca, l'imprenditore ha gettato la spugna.
exEn: After the bank's third refusal, the entrepreneur threw in the towel.
note: From boxing, like the English idiom. Also 'gettare le armi' (lay down arms), 'alzare bandiera bianca'.

en: be the third wheel; play gooseberry
ex: Non vengo al cinema con voi due: non ho voglia di reggere il moccolo tutta la sera.
exEn: I am not coming to the cinema with you two: I do not feel like being the third wheel all evening.
note: 'Moccolo' = candle stub: the servant holding the candle for lovers. Also 'tenere il moccolo'; 'tirare un moccolo' means instead to swear.

en: be in a foul temper; be hopping mad
ex: Lascialo stare oggi: ha un diavolo per capello dopo la riunione con il direttore.
exEn: Leave him alone today: he is in a foul temper after the meeting with the director.
note: Colloquial. Compare 'essere fuori di sé', 'essere nero' (regional), 'avere la luna storta' (grumpy).

en: look after one's own interests; put a spin that favours oneself
ex: Ogni ministro, in sede di bilancio, tira acqua al proprio mulino.
exEn: Every minister, at budget time, looks after his own interests.
note: Image: diverting the stream to power one's own mill. Mildly critical of self-interested argumentation.

it: restare con un palmo di naso
en: be left empty-handed and disappointed; be left looking foolish
ex: Pensava di ottenere la promozione, e invece è restato con un palmo di naso.
exEn: He thought he would get the promotion, and instead he was left empty-handed.
note: Also 'rimanere con un palmo di naso' or 'con tanto di naso'. Image: the long face of disappointment.

ex: Senza fondi per assumere, hanno fatto di necessità virtù automatizzando le procedure.
exEn: With no funds to hire, they made a virtue of necessity by automating the procedures.
note: Proverbial, from Latin; register is neutral to elevated. Compare 'fare buon viso a cattivo gioco'.

it: fare buon viso a cattivo gioco
en: put a brave face on it; grin and bear it
ex: Non era d'accordo con la decisione, ma ha fatto buon viso a cattivo gioco per non rompere con i soci.
exEn: He did not agree with the decision, but he put a brave face on it so as not to break with his partners.
note: From card games: keeping a pleasant face despite a bad hand. Often 'fare buon viso a cattiva sorte' in the variant with fate.

it: cavarsela per il rotto della cuffia
en: scrape through; get away by the skin of one's teeth
ex: Non aveva studiato quasi nulla, ma all'orale se l'è cavata per il rotto della cuffia.
exEn: He had hardly studied at all, but he scraped through the oral exam.
note: From medieval tournaments: a lance that only tore the 'cuffia' (cap under the helmet) did not count. Also 'passare/uscirne per il rotto della cuffia'.
